name: Fibromuscular Dysplasia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: No universally accepted formal criteria; diagnosis based on imaging and clinical features

criteria.description: Characteristic 'string of beads' appearance on angiography indicating arterial stenosis and aneurysmal dilatation
Presence of non-atherosclerotic, non-inflammatory arterial lesions affecting medium-sized arteries
Exclusion of atherosclerotic disease and vasculitis by clinical and laboratory evaluation
Clinical symptoms consistent with arterial stenosis, aneurysm, or dissection such as hypertension or ischemic symptoms

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic angiographic findings plus exclusion of atherosclerosis and vasculitis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on imaging modalities such as catheter-based angiography, CTA, or MRA.

searchTerms: string of beads pattern in blood vessels

pathognomonic.notes: Secondary hypertension due to renal artery involvement

common.notes: Often due to carotid or vertebral artery involvement
Related to arterial dissection or aneurysm

occasional.notes: From renal or mesenteric artery stenosis
From carotid or vertebral artery involvement

rare.notes: Due to arterial occlusion or embolism

imaging: Catheter-based angiography showing 'string of beads' pattern
CT angiography (CTA) and MR angiography (MRA) demonstrating arterial stenosis and aneurysms
genetic: No definitive genetic mutation identified; familial cases reported suggesting possible genetic predisposition
other: Histopathology (rarely performed) shows medial fibroplasia with alternating areas of fibrosis and thinning

distinguishingFeatures: Elevated lipid levels and cardiovascular risk factors
Systemic symptoms such as fever and weight loss
Histopathologic evidence of vessel wall inflammation
Connective tissue disorder with systemic features
Aortic root dilation rather than medium artery involvement
Genetic testing positive for FBN1 mutations

redFlags: Sudden onset severe headache or neurological deficit indicating possible arterial dissection or stroke
Rapidly worsening hypertension refractory to medical therapy
Signs of arterial rupture or aneurysm rupture such as sudden severe pain and hypotension
references: Olin JW, Gornik HL, Bacharach JM, et al. Fibromuscular Dysplasia: State of the Science and Critical Unanswered Questions: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association. Circulation. 2014;129(9):1048-1078.
Plouin PF, Baguet JP, Thony F, et al. Fibromuscular dysplasia. Orphanet J Rare Dis. 2007;2:28.
Gornik HL, Persu A, Adlam D, et al. First International Consensus on the diagnosis and management of fibromuscular dysplasia. Vasc Med. 2019;24(2):164-189.
